questions: Did the tremor and coordination problems begin suddenly, over minutes to hours?
Have they been steadily worsening since they began?
Have you ever had similar neurological episodes that later improved?
Did the symptoms begin after a head injury?
Have you had a recent stroke or transient ischaemic attack?
Do you have weakness or numbness on one side of your body?
Do you have double vision or difficulty controlling your eye movements?
Have you had episodes of vision loss or painful loss of vision in one eye?
Do you have problems with bladder control or marked urinary urgency?
Have you had slurred speech or difficulty swallowing?
Have you had severe or new headaches, vomiting, or worsening symptoms when lying down?
Have you experienced seizures, confusion, or changes in personality?
Do close relatives have tremor, poor coordination, or a similar neurological disorder?
Do you regularly drink substantial amounts of alcohol?
Has the tremor become worse after recently reducing or stopping alcohol?
Have you started or increased any medication before the symptoms began?
Do you use lithium, valproate, phenytoin, metoclopramide, or amiodarone?
Have you been exposed to solvents, mercury, lead, or other industrial toxins?
Do you have a history of cancer?
Have you recently had a significant infection or fever?
Have you had unexplained weight loss or night sweats?
Do you have liver disease?
Do you have thyroid disease or symptoms such as palpitations, heat intolerance, or unexplained weight loss?
Did the symptoms begin before age 25?
Do you have difficulty walking even when you are not experiencing the tremor?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: POU4F1-related autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia (POU4F1-associated SCA50) caused by a heterozygous pathogenic loss-of-function nonsense variant

Alternative: Another genetically undefined autosomal dominant spinocerebellar ataxia

Alternative: An atypical repeat-expansion spinocerebellar ataxia not detected by the performed testing

Alternative: RFC1-associated late-onset ataxia, although unlikely given the phenotype and reported genetic findings
